newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: OLYMPICS-NAGANO DOWNHILL DISPUTE TO BE SETTLED NEXT MONTH.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-NAGANO DOWNHILL DISPUTE TO BE SETTLED NEXT MONTH.

text.p: A dispute over the venue of the downhill ski events at the 1998 Winter Olympics will be settled within a month, Marc Hodler, president of the International Ski Federation (FIS), said on Saturday.

Nagano officials have refused an FIS request to raise the start of the downhill course to 1,800 metres above sea level from the current 1,680 metres because that would push the course into a national park.
Nagano organisers suggested to FIS that if it was unhappy with the course the downhills could be staged in two heats.
But FIS quickly rejected this idea, saying it would even consider holding the downhills outside Japan.
"There is nothing new about the issue," said Hodler. "The question is whether we will be able to oppose militant Japanese environmentalists."

Hodler was in Maribor to see IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch receive a high state award from Slovenian president Milan Kucan, marking the country's independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991.
